sentences.zh: 如果你确实有一个在生命中某个阶段对你进行过虐待的父母或照顾者，真的值得花时间深入研究一下，问问自己，

sentences.en: And if you do have a parent or a caregiver that was abusive towards you at some point in your life, it's really worth your time to look deeper into that and ask yourself,
sentences.zh: 这如何促成了我现在让事情就这样发生在我生活中，而不去质疑任何事情的方式？

sentences.en: how has this enabled the way that I now allow things to just land in my life and not question any of it?
sentences.zh: 当我在那些表现出某些相似之处的男性身边时，我是如何运作的，这些相似之处激发了我证明自己值得被爱的本能？

sentences.en: How do I operate when I'm around men who present certain similarities that fire up this instinct in me to prove that I'm worthy of love?
sentences.zh: 我能做些什么来开始练习那种离开对我不好的人的冒险感觉？

sentences.en: And what can I do to start practicing that risky feeling of walking away from men who aren't good for me?
sentences.zh: 因为讽刺的是，一旦你从生命中主要的痛苦源头分离出来，如果那个主要的痛苦源头来自父母，

sentences.en: Because ironically, once you've separated from the main source of pain in your life, if that main source of pain comes from a parent,
sentences.zh: 其他一切都变得更容易离开了。

sentences.en: everything else becomes easier to walk away from.
sentences.zh: 这就是我认为很多人正在挣扎的原因，因为他们没有消除那种深层痛苦、深层创伤、深层触发的主要源头。

sentences.en: And that's what I think a lot of people are struggling with because they haven't eliminated the main source of that deep pain, that deep trauma, that deep trigger.
sentences.zh: 他们仍然被那些重要性甚至不到最初创造这些触发因素的主要照顾者一半的人所触发。

sentences.en: They're still getting re-triggered by people who don't even hold half the importance that the primary caregiver that initially created those triggers even hold in their life.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: Oh my gosh.
sentences.zh: 而且，我认为你说得完全正确。

sentences.en: And that's, I think you're absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 这在很多方面完全可以用心理学来解释。

sentences.en: It completely is explained in many ways by psychology.
sentences.zh: 我想说，你做出那个决定非常了不起，因为我们寻求父母，特别是在童年早期和早期发展阶段，寻求一切。

sentences.en: And I think just to say so much credit to you for making that decision, because we look to our parents, especially in early childhood and in our early development for everything.
sentences.zh: 他们是我们生命的源泉，这就解释了为什么当我们决定需要与他们决裂时，如果那是你需要做的事情，那将会非常痛苦。

sentences.en: They are our source of life, and that explains why when we decide that we need to make that break from them, if that's something that you need to do, it's going to be so painful.
sentences.zh: 那是主要的痛苦，对吧？

sentences.en: That's the primary pain, right?
sentences.zh: 那是第一轮。

sentences.en: That's the first round.
sentences.zh: 然后第二轮来自于不得不去学习他们隐晦地、潜意识地教给你的关于你值得什么的东西。

sentences.en: And then the second round comes from having to unlearn what they've taught you implicitly and subconsciously about what you deserve.
sentences.zh: 每当我想到这些事情，每当我与像你这样的人交谈或对此进行研究时，我总是会想到一句名言，

sentences.en: And there's a quote I always think of whenever I think about these things, whenever I speak to people like yourself or do research on this,
sentences.zh: 那就是我们在成年关系中寻求的是我们童年时期所没有的东西。

sentences.en: and it's that what we seek in our adult relationships is what we didn't have as children.
sentences.zh: 而且它不仅限于此，我们在浪漫伴侣、男性、女性或其他任何人身上建立的关系，都会复制我们早期的父母关系。

sentences.en: And it goes beyond that in that the relationships we have with our romantic partners, men, women, whoever, will replicate those early parental relationships we have.
sentences.zh: 而且它不仅限于此，我们在浪漫伴侣、男性、女性或其他任何人身上建立的关系，都会复制我们早期的父母关系。

sentences.en: Because that is the model.
sentences.zh: 因为那就是范本。

sentences.en: That is the model for how we love ourselves.
sentences.zh: 那是我们如何爱自己的范本。

sentences.en: That is the model for how we let others treat ourselves.
sentences.zh: 那是我们如何让别人对待自己的范本。

sentences.en: And the influence on our adult relationships is just – it cannot be forgotten, and I don't think it can be downgraded at all.
sentences.zh: 它对我们成年后人际关系的影响是——它无法被遗忘，而且我认为它根本无法被低估。

sentences.en: And exactly what you said, right?
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，对吧？

sentences.en: You find that when you are able to detach from that primary caregiver,
sentences.zh: 你会发现，当你能够与那位主要照料者分离时，

sentences.en: it becomes a lot easier to stand up for yourself in other relationships because you have already made that decision.
sentences.zh: 在其他人际关系中坚持自我就会变得容易得多，因为你已经做出了那个决定。

sentences.en: You have already – it couldn't hurt you anymore.
sentences.zh: 你已经——它再也伤害不了你了。

sentences.en: Your primary relationship with your caregiver or whoever it may be, your guardian, is one of the most fundamental.
sentences.zh: 你与照料者或无论那是谁，你的监护人之间的主要关系，是最根本的关系之一。

sentences.en: Everything else is in some ways secondary.
sentences.zh: 其他一切在某种程度上都是次要的。

sentences.en: I do have a question, though, because there's probably people listening to this who can really identify with you and be like, I actually need to do that.
sentences.zh: 不过我有一个问题，因为可能有人在听这段对话时，能真正与你产生共鸣，心想：我确实需要这样做。

sentences.en: That's – my relationship with my mother or my father or my guardian is really similar.
sentences.zh: 那就是——我和我母亲、父亲或监护人的关系真的很相似。

sentences.en: Do you have any tips?
sentences.zh: 你有什么建议吗？

sentences.en: Like, how did you go about that?
sentences.zh: 比如，你是怎么处理这件事的？

sentences.en: And what did you find were some of those key lessons that you learned along the way?
sentences.zh: 你觉得在这一过程中学到的关键经验有哪些？

sentences.en: So I'd say for anybody who might be listening and resonating and thinking, wow, this sounds like me.
sentences.zh: 所以我想对任何可能正在收听、产生共鸣并心想“哇，这听起来像我”的人说：

sentences.en: I think I've tolerated abuse from someone who was supposed to protect me and nurture me and love me.
sentences.zh: 我想我一直忍受着本该保护我、养育我、爱我的人的虐待。

sentences.en: Well, when I was in the initial stage of, first of all, believing myself and believing that, yes, this is abuse,
sentences.zh: 嗯，当我处于最初阶段时，首先是相信自己，相信“是的，这就是虐待”，

sentences.en: I didn't go down the route of confronting the person and being like, I've figured out what you're up to.
sentences.zh: 我并没有走去和那个人对质，说“我已经发现你的企图了”那条路。

sentences.en: I know you're trying to break me.
sentences.zh: 我知道你想摧毁我。

sentences.en: Instead, I chose to give myself all the time I needed to mentally detach before I ended up eventually physically moving out.
sentences.zh: 相反，我选择给自己所有需要的时间在心理上进行分离，直到最终搬出去。

sentences.en: The mental detachment process was the longest and hardest, and I would say that process never entirely really ends.
sentences.zh: 心理分离的过程是最漫长、最艰难的，而且我想说这个过程永远不会真正彻底结束。

sentences.en: But how I approached that process was I started to really – this is what I'm grateful for with YouTube.
sentences.zh: 但我处理这个过程的方法是，我开始真正地——这就是我感谢 YouTube 的地方。

sentences.en: There are so many people on there who share their own personal accounts about living with a narcissistic parent,
sentences.zh: 上面有很多人分享他们自己与自恋型父母生活的亲身经历，

sentences.en: living with a controlling parent, living with an abuser, and when I would watch those people's videos,
sentences.zh: 与控制型父母生活，与施虐者生活，当我观看那些人的视频时，

sentences.en: I would notice so many similarities in what I was experiencing, and then I started to believe, oh, this is real, and this is not an isolated experience.
sentences.zh: 我注意到我所经历的事情有太多相似之处，然后我开始相信，哦，这是真实的，这不是孤立的经历。

sentences.en: Okay, now the next step has to be really getting to the nucleus of this.
sentences.zh: 好了，下一步必须是真正触及问题的核心。

sentences.en: Like, why would somebody behave like this?
sentences.zh: 比如，为什么会有人表现得像这样？

sentences.en: Because now that I know that it's not because of me, I want to understand the background of that person,
sentences.zh: 因为既然我知道这不是我的原因，我想了解那个人的背景，

sentences.en: not to justify or support their behavior, but to understand the scale of what kind of almost monster I'm working with,
sentences.zh: 不是为了证明或支持他们的行为，而是为了了解我所面对的几乎是怪物级别的人，

sentences.en: because it feels like the person you love has been taken over by a monster that isn't them.
sentences.zh: 因为感觉就像你爱的人被一个不是他们自己的怪物占据了。

sentences.en: That was how I used to see it as a child.
sentences.zh: 小时候我就是这么看的。

sentences.en: I used to just think that a monster has mounted my mom, and that's why she hates me.
sentences.zh: 我过去常认为有一个怪物骑在我妈妈身上，所以她才恨我。

sentences.en: Oh my gosh.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: Right, and so when I would research and see that, okay, this is a cycle of trauma, this is not entirely to do with me, but unfortunately I am a reflection of my caregiver,
sentences.zh: 没错，所以当我研究并发现，好吧，这是一个创伤循环，这并不完全与我有关，但遗憾的是我是我照料者的映射，

sentences.en: so they are going to upload their trauma onto me.
sentences.zh: 所以他们会把他们的创伤投射到我身上。

sentences.en: Well, now I have to start putting myself in self-protection mode, because I'm an adult and I need to see that there is a four-year-old child visual of me,
sentences.zh: 好吧，现在我必须开始进入自我保护模式，因为我是成年人了，我需要看到我内心有一个四岁的孩子，

sentences.en: and I need to step in and protect that child.
sentences.zh: 我需要介入并保护那个孩子。

sentences.en: So I did everything I could to equip myself with all of the psychological knowledge and support
sentences.zh: 所以我尽我所能用我需要的所有心理知识和支持来武装自己，

sentences.en: I would need to justify leaving, because there were so many times I almost talked myself out of it.
sentences.zh: 以证明离开是合理的，因为有太多次我差点说服自己放弃。

sentences.en: And this is why people say that it takes, on average, what's the statistic?
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么人们说平均需要——那个统计数据是多少？

sentences.en: I think it takes, on average, like, is it seven or ten attempts to leave an abuser?
sentences.zh: 我想平均需要，比如，是七次还是十次才能离开施虐者？

sentences.en: Yeah, it's as high as, like, 20 sometimes.
sentences.zh: 是的，有时高达 20 次。

sentences.en: Like, it can take as many times as it takes.
sentences.zh: 就像，可能需要多少次就得多少次。

sentences.en: And it took me quite a while to get over the emotion of feeling guilty.
sentences.zh: 我花了好长一段时间才克服那种内疚感。

sentences.en: I think guilt is what stops most people from leaving, because you feel like now that you've researched and you've got all this information
sentences.zh: 我认为内疚是阻止大多数人离开的原因，因为你会觉得既然你已经研究过了，也得到了所有这些信息，

sentences.en: and you've noticed that, oh, wow, this person is doing this, not because they are an inherently evil person,
sentences.zh: 并且你注意到，哦，哇，这个人这样做，不是因为他们本质上是个坏人，

sentences.en: but because there's something that's gone wrong somewhere down the line for them, and they just never made the choice to address it.
sentences.zh: 而是因为他们在某个地方出了问题，而他们从未做出选择去解决它。

sentences.en: You start to feel bad for that person, and then you start to justify, and then you start to tell yourself, well, they haven't really got anyone else but me.
sentences.zh: 你开始为那个人感到难过，然后你开始找借口，然后你开始告诉自己，好吧，他们除了我真的没有别人了。

sentences.en: But there's a reason why they haven't got anyone else but you, and that's because they have destroyed all their relationships, and you are up next.
sentences.zh: 但他们除了你没有别人是有原因的，那是因为他们摧毁了他们所有的关系，而你就是下一个。

sentences.en: So I stopped feeling as guilty, and I think something a lot of people are worried about, and this is ironically why most women just tolerate really horrible men,
sentences.zh: 所以我不再那么内疚了，我认为很多人担心的一件事——讽刺的是，这也是大多数女性只是忍受非常糟糕的男人的原因——

sentences.en: is because you feel like if you really were to believe yourself and explicitly trust your observations, you feel like you're going to stop being the nice person that you are,
sentences.zh: 是因为你觉得如果你真的相信自己并明确信任你的观察，你会觉得你将不再是你那个善良的人，

sentences.en: because the idea of putting yourself first and leaving somebody right in their tracks when they don't expect it feels as evil as the abuser abusing you,
sentences.zh: 因为把你自己放在首位，在某人意想不到的时候离开他们，感觉就像施虐者虐待你一样邪恶，

sentences.en: and that's a false equivalence that we create, almost as a way to kind of create an excuse for yourself to still stay longer,
sentences.zh: 这是一种我们创造的虚假等同，几乎是为了给自己找借口继续停留更长时间，

sentences.en: but also because it's really scary to live life on the other side where you've never known an existence that doesn't involve your primary caregiver's abuse.
sentences.zh: 但也因为生活在另一面真的很可怕，在那里你从未经历过没有主要照料者虐待的生活。

sentences.en: It feels like it's safer to just stay in the abuse and tell yourself that there's ways to work around it.
sentences.zh: 感觉留在虐待中并告诉自己有办法绕过它更安全。

sentences.en: You can just put your headphones in and ignore the shouting, or you can always just keep on living a double life, and it's not worth it.
sentences.zh: 你可以戴上耳机忽略叫喊声，或者你可以一直过着双重生活，但这不值得。

sentences.en: I think if people were to be told
sentences.zh: 我想如果人们被告知

sentences.en: exactly how many days they have left on this earth, like if we were all walking around with a floating number above our heads that said how many days we have left on this earth,
sentences.zh: 他们在这个世界上还剩下多少天，就像我们所有人头顶都漂浮着一个数字，显示我们在这个世界上还剩下多少天，

sentences.en: I think most of us would make the decision quicker to cut ties because it's like living your life on half speed, just like having an abuser in your life
sentences.zh: 我想我们大多数人会更快地做出切断联系的决定，因为这就像以半速生活，就像生活中有一个施虐者，

sentences.en: who knows that they have access to you because they gave birth to you and because they can.
sentences.zh: 他知道他可以接触到你，因为他生了你，而且因为他能做到。

sentences.en: And when it comes to being a woman that dates men and feeling bad about leaving men behind, you have nothing to feel bad about.
sentences.zh: 当谈到作为一个与男性约会的女性，并为离开男性而感到难过时，你没什么可难过的。

sentences.en: We as women who date men feel guilty about even daring to have a particular standard or having any kind of taste.
sentences.zh: 我们作为与男性约会的女性，甚至为敢于拥有某种标准或拥有任何品味而感到内疚。

sentences.en: So it's like going back to my initial point of what you learnt to tolerate as a child will definitely set the tone for what you believe you're deserving of,
sentences.zh: 所以这就像回到我最初的观点，你小时候学会忍受的东西肯定会为你认为自己值得什么定下基调，

sentences.en: and you have to quite literally go out of your way to make the effort to break that cycle of thinking, and it's going to feel unnatural.
sentences.zh: 你必须真正地不遗余力地去打破那种思维循环，这会让你感到不自然。

sentences.en: But just because it feels unnatural doesn't mean that it's wrong.
sentences.zh: 但仅仅因为它感觉不自然并不意味着它是错的。

sentences.en: I think that is so difficult.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这太难了。

sentences.en: Like what you said, where it's like it, like we said, it takes so many times to leave an abusive situation.
sentences.zh: 就像你说的，就像我们说的，离开虐待环境需要很多次。

sentences.en: There's so many reasons behind this, right?
sentences.zh: 这背后有很多原因，对吧？

sentences.en: They hijack our brains.
sentences.zh: 他们劫持了我们的大脑。

sentences.en: There is a feeling that becomes associated with that person, and it's not just fear.
sentences.zh: 有一种与那个人相关的感觉，不仅仅是恐惧。

sentences.en: It's not just worry or being scared.
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是担心或害怕。

sentences.en: There's also the other hand, like the other side of the coin, right?
sentences.zh: 还有另一面，就像硬币的另一面，对吧？

sentences.en: It's how amazing it feels to be loved by them in the moments where they're not harming you, where they're not controlling you.
sentences.zh: 在他们不伤害你、不控制你的时刻，被他们爱着的感觉是多么美妙。

sentences.en: And something that I think isn't often acknowledged is how much that is part of the abusive process.
sentences.zh: 我认为有一点经常被忽视，那就是这在多大程度上是虐待过程的一部分。

sentences.en: You know, you spoke about financial abuse, emotional abuse, social abuse, cognitive abuse.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你谈到了经济虐待、情感虐待、社会虐待、认知虐待。

sentences.en: All of those things are things that are, in many ways, identical to the abuse that you would experience from a partner.
sentences.zh: 所有这些事情在许多方面与你从伴侣那里经历的虐待是相同的。

sentences.en: But it's coming from a primary caregiver.
sentences.zh: 但它来自主要照料者。

sentences.en: You don't get another parent.
sentences.zh: 你没有第二个父母。

sentences.en: You know, you don't get another chance at that parental relationship, which was why I'm sure it would have hurt so, so much.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你没有第二次机会去建立那种亲子关系，这就是为什么我敢肯定那会非常、非常痛苦。

sentences.en: But on the other side of the coin is,
sentences.zh: 但在硬币的另一面是，

sentences.en: I'm sure there were probably moments in which you were like, oh, but maybe this is all right.
sentences.zh: 我敢肯定可能有一些时刻你会想，哦，但也许这还可以。

sentences.en: Maybe I can deal with this.
sentences.zh: 也许我能应付这个。

sentences.en: You know, I'm reliant on them for some form of security, some form of comfort.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我在某种形式的安全感、某种形式的安慰上依赖他们。

sentences.en: Um, and I think that the other really important point that you raised there, which I think is so, so pertinent to what we're talking about today
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为你提出的另一个非常重要的观点，我认为与我们今天讨论的内容非常、非常相关，

sentences.en: is how it creates our attachment style, right?
sentences.zh: 那就是它如何创造了我们的依恋类型，对吧？

sentences.en: Like the relationship you have with your parent, the relationship you have with your primary caregiver, it is going to directly input and impact
sentences.zh: 就像你与父母的关系，你与主要照料者的关系，它将直接输入并影响

sentences.en: how you're going to attach yourselves, not just to romantic interests, but to friends, to locations, to cities, to jobs.
sentences.zh: 你将如何依恋，不仅是对浪漫对象，还有朋友、地点、城市、工作。

sentences.en: Because if you've been taught that love is not freely given, you're never going to expect that.
sentences.zh: 因为如果你被教导爱不是自由给予的，你永远不会期待它。

sentences.en: And you're never going to welcome that because that feels like fear to you.
sentences.zh: 而且你永远不会欢迎它，因为那对你来说感觉像恐惧。

sentences.en: And like I was saying, you know, someone gives you that attention, someone gives you that love, someone gives you that comfort.
sentences.zh: 就像我说的，你知道，有人给你那种关注，有人给你那种爱，有人给你那种安慰。

sentences.en: In your previous situations with your primary caregiver, you know what's coming next.
sentences.zh: 在你之前与主要照料者的处境中，你知道接下来会发生什么。

sentences.en: There's never love without fear.
sentences.zh: 没有恐惧就没有爱。

sentences.en: There's never love without hurt.
sentences.zh: 没有伤害就没有爱。

sentences.en: And so when you grow up, when you become an adult, when you start to make your own family or make your own decisions around who's in your life,
sentences.zh: 所以当你长大，当你成为成年人，当你开始组建自己的家庭或围绕谁出现在你的生活中做出自己的决定时，

sentences.en: there'll be people who are going to offer you love and who are going to really care about you.
sentences.zh: 会有一些人愿意给你爱，并且会真正关心你。

sentences.en: And there's always that fear, right?
sentences.zh: 但总是有那种恐惧，对吧？

sentences.en: That's kind of in the back of your mind.
